scenario.name: f05-gravity-turn
assumptions: Single-stage gravity-turn study of the F-02 reference plant and the F-04 tracker with the packaged illustrative spike_stage aero -- illustrative vehicle, not flight-certified.

Both models share the identical vehicle object, physics switches (US76 + J2 + rotation), ambient-corrected engine law, attitude program and RK4 core; the pair differs only in the 6-DOF content the attribution ladder isolates.
Constant full throttle until propellant exhaustion, then coast; throttle scheduling is guidance (F-06/F-07), not this study.

attitude_dynamics.description: rigid-body inertia + discrete tracker, aero off both sides (6dof_ideal - 3dof_vacuum)

actuator_lag.description: TVC first-order lag + slew limit on the aero-off loop (6dof_lag - 6dof_ideal)

aero_rigid_body.description: body-oriented aero on the lagged 6-DOF loop (6dof_full - 6dof_lag)

aero_point_mass.description: drag/lift carried by the 3-DOF baseline, the headline's counter-term (3dof_aero - 3dof_vacuum)

checks.rationale: the tracker must hold the body on the program inside 6 deg while it has thrust; a whole-run maximum is not a control requirement because the coast is unactuated by design (the tracker trims to neutral at MECO)
the mean of the same error over the burn, on the same authority argument
the packaged spike_stage coefficient tables end at +/-15 deg AoA: beyond them the aero model is clamped extrapolation, so the loaded phase must stay inside the envelope the coefficients describe
q*alpha is this study's side-load proxy (the bending/side load the airframe sees); the 500 kPa-deg budget is the study-level structural allowance E1-02 declares for the booster
at least 90 % of the +/-5 deg gimbal travel in reserve while the engine is lit: the tracker must be steering, not running out of authority
the same reserve on the yaw axis
zero seconds of travel saturation in the powered phase: a saturated gimbal means the command exceeded the actuator, i.e. the loop asked for something the vehicle cannot deliver
the same on the yaw axis
zero seconds of rate saturation in the powered phase: the program's pitch-over here is slow enough that the gimbal rate limit is never the binding constraint
the same on the yaw axis
the coast phase of this scenario is above ~100 km, so it must be an *unloaded* phase: this is what licenses reading the large coast attitude/AoA numbers as geometry rather than as loads
the same argument in load terms: even the worst coast side load must be three orders below the powered budget

the reported burn time must be the burn, not the flight span (task #251: the study used to report tvc.burn_s = 180.0 for a 99.85 s burn): within 1 % of the event-detected propellant exhaustion, the gap being tick granularity

the two backends must agree on the *loaded* phase: the whole-run alpha discrepancy is a coast-phase artifact, so if it ever reappears in the powered window this line fails instead of being hidden by a headline number

the 6-DOF whole-run alpha_max must belong to the coast phase (it is the ballistic attitude drift of an unactuated, un-loaded body): if a future change makes the powered peak the larger one, this line flips and the explanation above has to be rewritten
